quarterly_data.signal: Head of IR Susie Lisa said the AMPLITUDE phase III interim analysis of inaxaplin in AMKD comes in the first quarter of 2027 at a 48-week endpoint; the accelerated approval endpoint is the change in eGFR from baseline, plus the reduction in proteinuria. Vertex will disclose the 48-week eGFR and, if successful, continue to follow patients for the full two-year endpoint, and it would likely be Vertex's second commercial launch in renal. She said AMKD patients lose eGFR about 50% faster than typical CKD patients, about 6 or 7 per year versus 3 or 4, and that inaxaplin delivers 98% plus inhibition of APOL1, which underpins Vertex's optimism for the modest-proteinuria cohort.
quarterly_data.figure: interim analysis in the first quarter of 2027 at 48 weeks; eGFR loss about 6 or 7 per year versus 3 or 4 for typical CKD; 98% plus APOL1 inhibition

quarterly_data.signal: Susie Lisa said that in IgAN the U.S. FDA clearly will accept one-year eGFR data but other global regulators will not; there is no path to accelerated approval in Europe, and there are more IgAN patients in Asia than in the U.S. and Europe combined, which Vertex is weighing in deciding disclosures and timing on povetacicept. She expects physicians initially to target higher-proteinuria patients, with that coming down over time as KDIGO guidelines push toward the 0.5 proteinuria threshold and concurrent rather than serial treatment, and said Vertex will go after both switchers and de novo patients.

Susie Lisa said JOURNAVX has north of 36,000 prescribers. The acute pain market is about one third hospital and two thirds home or retail, while Vertex's mix remains closer to 50/50 because it focuses on in-hospital prescribers; the average hospital script is in the 2- to 5-day range versus about 14 days for retail. She said the lag in revenue recognition versus what Vertex initially hoped reflects reimbursed-access delays, with the patient support program still triggered at retail when parent-plan coverage has not yet been implemented at the child-plan level or by quantity-limit and prior-authorization technicalities; Vertex will keep the PSP in place and expects a more normalized gross to net around mid-2027, probably something in a plus or minus 50% range.
quarterly_data.figure: north of 36,000 prescribers; market about one third hospital, two thirds retail versus Vertex mix about 50/50; hospital script 2- to 5-day, retail 14-day; gross to net plus or minus 50% around mid-2027

quarterly_data.signal: Susie Lisa said the suzetrigine phase II in diabetic peripheral neuropathy showed greater than a 2-point improvement in NPRS, and the two phase III DPN studies, run at a controlled number of experienced sites with significant placebo-management training, should put Vertex on pace for data sometime in the first half of 2027, likely. In myasthenia gravis the 12-week povetacicept phase II of about 30 patients is enrolling, with no timelines given, but she called it a catalyst probably over the next 12 months or so; Vertex sees a BAFF-APRIL inhibitor as a chronic therapy without the cycling on and off needed with other therapies.
quarterly_data.figure: greater than a 2-point NPRS improvement in phase II; DPN data likely in the first half of 2027; MG phase II about 30 patients over 12 weeks, catalyst over the next 12 months or so

quarterly_data.signal: Susie Lisa on the approximate $5 billion Crinetics peak sales figure: PALSONIFY, approved for acromegaly and off to a great start, is a blockbuster opportunity that Vertex aims to accelerate and expand outside the U.S., while atumelnant in congenital adrenal hyperplasia is the larger, multi-billion dollar opportunity; atumelnant is also being studied in Cushing's disease, which could provide additional upside, and the $5 billion does not include the early-stage assets. Updated guidance and financial impact will come next quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: approximate $5 billion peak sales, excluding early-stage assets
